<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="סיון_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918872_theRebbe_254" batchId="meluket-_D7_A1_D7_99_D7_95_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918872_theRebbe_254__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Love and will are still a finite existence, whereas true self-nullification is the service of accepting the yoke, like a servant with no will of his own, and this aspect of nullification is inherited from the Patriarchs who were the Merkavah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it is known,</t>
    <t s="1">that love is the love and will of the person</t>
    <t s="2">(the lover),</t>
    <t s="3">and therefore,</t>
    <t s="4">even when his love and will is that the Supernal will be fulfilled,</t>
    <t s="5">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="6">the essential concept of love and will is an existence.</t>
    <t s="7">And the true concept of nullification is in the service of accepting the yoke,</t>
    <t s="8">which is like a servant who has no desires whatsoever,</t>
    <t s="9">and everything he does is because of the yoke of the master that is upon him,</t>
    <t s="10">by virtue of which he is compelled to fulfill the will of the master.</t>
    <t s="11">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="12">that since the nullification of the chariot to the rider is not from the will of the chariot</t>
    <t s="13">(that it wants to be nullified to the rider and be a chariot for him),</t>
    <t s="14">but rather from the rider,</t>
    <t s="15">therefore, in the inheritance from the Patriarchs, who are the Merkavah, there is also included in concealment the nullification of accepting the yoke.</t>
    <t s="16">[And one may note from the saying of our sages, of blessed memory,</t>
    <t s="17">"At the time that Israel preceded 'we will do' to 'we will hear'... who revealed this secret to My children?" And it is explained in Chassidus</t>
    <t s="18">that this precedence of "we will do" to "we will hear"</t>
    <t s="19">[that in the nullification of accepting the yoke itself, there is a most elevated nullification,</t>
    <t s="20">nullification to the Master of Will]</t>
    <t s="21">is through the revelation of the hidden love,</t>
    <t s="22">a secret.</t>
    <t s="23">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="24">that the connection of the hidden love</t>
    <t s="25">(existence)</t>
    <t s="26">to the precedence of "we will do" to "we will hear"</t>
    <t s="27">(nullification of accepting the yoke),</t>
    <t s="28">is,</t>
    <t s="29">that the hidden love is an inheritance from the Patriarchs, who are the Merkavah].</t>
    <t s="30">And from this it is understood,</t>
    <t s="31">that the nullification drawn down to Israel at the giving of the Torah</t>
    <t s="32">(after they preceded "we will do" to "we will hear")</t>
    <t s="33">is a nullification more elevated even than the nullification of the Merkavah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The "Great Matter" is the Work of the Chariot, which elevates from the limited level of "Man" to the unlimited level of "Not-Man," specifically through the Chariot of the Patriarchs in Atzilus.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="2">that it is stated in the Gemara,</t>
    <t s="3">"They said about Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai that he did not leave out anything great or anything small—</t>
    <t s="4">'a great matter' is the Work of the Chariot, 'a small matter' is the discussions of Abaye and Rava."</t>
    <t s="5">And it is explained in the Maamar,</t>
    <t s="6">that the reason the Work of the Chariot is called a "great matter" is,</t>
    <t s="7">that through the chariot,</t>
    <t s="8">the person riding upon the chariot reaches a place he cannot reach on his own,</t>
    <t s="9">and likewise is it in the Supernal Chariot,</t>
    <t s="10">that the Chayos bear the Throne</t>
    <t s="11">and the Man upon the Throne</t>
    <t s="12">to the level of "Not-Man."</t>
    <t s="13">And the main elevation to the level of "Not-Man" is through the Chariot of the Patriarchs</t>
    <t s="14">(the Patriarchs, they are the Merkavah),</t>
    <t s="15">the Chariot of Atzilus.</t>
    <t s="16">For the elevation of the level of "Man" to the level of "Not-Man" that is through the Chariot of BY"A is that the Man upon the Throne</t>
    <t s="17">(the Man of BY"A)</t>
    <t s="18">is elevated to a level that is a level of "Not-Man" relative to the Man of BY"A,</t>
    <t s="19">and through the Chariot of the Patriarchs,</t>
    <t s="20">the Chariot of Atzilus,</t>
    <t s="21">there is an elevation of the level of Man of Atzilus to the level of "Not-Man" that is above Atzilus,</t>
    <t s="22">Arich.</t>
    <t s="23">And this is that the Work of the Chariot is called a "great matter,"</t>
    <t s="24">for Man,</t>
    <t s="25">Zeir Anpin,</t>
    <t s="26">is a level of smallness and contraction,</t>
    <t s="27">and through the Chariot he is elevated to the level of Arich,</t>
    <t s="28">Great.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The discussions of Abaye and Rava are called a "small matter" because the laws of the Torah are clothed in small, limited things, and the Torah itself is a parable and garment for the Ein Sof, which is a small thing relative to the inner essence of Torah to be revealed in the future.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And the reason that the discussions of Abaye and Rava are called a "small matter"</t>
    <t s="1">(even though they are the essence of the Oral Torah)</t>
    <t s="2">is,</t>
    <t s="3">that the laws of the Torah are clothed in small things.</t>
    <t s="4">For in addition to the fact that the mitzvos are clothed in physical things,</t>
    <t s="5">each mitzvah has many particular laws,</t>
    <t s="6">for the concept of division</t>
    <t s="7">(particulars)</t>
    <t s="8">is contraction and limitation,</t>
    <t s="9">smallness.</t>
    <t s="10">[And based on this,</t>
    <t s="11">the difference between the Work of the Chariot and the discussions of Abaye and Rava is from one extreme to the other.</t>
    <t s="12">For the concept of the Chariot is the departure from the level of limitation</t>
    <t s="13">(Man)</t>
    <t s="14">to the level of without limitation</t>
    <t s="15">(Not-Man)</t>
    <t s="16">— a great matter</t>
    <t s="17">(for the true concept of greatness is in something that is not limited),</t>
    <t s="18">and in the discussions of Abaye and Rava it is the opposite,</t>
    <t s="19">the clothing of the Supernal Will,</t>
    <t s="20">which is without limit,</t>
    <t s="21">in limited things — a small matter].</t>
    <t s="22">And the Maamar continues with another reason for this, that the discussions of Abaye and Rava are called a "small matter,"</t>
    <t s="23">because the Torah of now is a small thing relative to the inner aspect of the Torah that will be revealed in the future.</t>
    <t s="24">And also because the Torah is a parable and garment for the Ein Sof that is clothed within it.</t>
    <t s="25">Therefore the Torah is called "the parable of the Ancient One,"</t>
    <t s="26">for it is a parable and garment for the level of the "Ancient One of the World."</t>
    <t s="27">And a parable relative to the thing being parabled is a small thing.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
